messages:
maria_zhou: Quick proposal: introduce a narrow \"golden path\" for telemetry attributes. Enforce low-cardinality primitives + explicit opt-ins for expensive/high-cardinality fields. Main objective: stable cost attribution + predictable observability costs.

sam_kapoor: 👍 can you list the exact primitives we expect?

maria_zhou: minimal required attributes: service, env, route, hashed_customer_id, request_type. All other fields must go into an optional metadata blob or be behind a per-tenant opt-in. Limit of 3 freeform customer-visible keys per span/event.

james: enforcement strategy? SDKs + CI + ingest?

maria_zhou: three tiers: 1) SDK lint that warns locally; 2) CI/PR checks that block new high-cardinality attributes in public SDKs; 3) ingest-side guardrails that trim/label exceeding keys and emit governance metrics. devops-bot: note: guardrails are feature-flagged at canary regions.

linh_tran: partners sometimes need lots of attributes for billing or reconciliation. How do we support them?

maria_zhou: partner opt-in via a signed allowlist. Per-tenant attribute quotas and an explicit billing_tag will ensure attribution accuracy for paying partners. Default behavior is strict.

sam_kapoor: sampling interactions are tricky. If we sample traces, heavy tenants could be undercounted.

maria_zhou: plan: make sampling tenant-aware. Deterministic sampling (or 100% sampling) for billing-critical tenants; statistical sampling for general telemetry. All sampled traces must include sampling_probability so analytics can reweight estimates.

james: can you show a simple reweighting example?

maria_zhou: ```sql
-- example reweighting
SUM(cost * (1.0 / sampling_probability)) AS estimated_cost
WHERE sampling_probability IS NOT NULL
```

linh_tran: rollout plan? Changing span schema is risky for many consumers.

maria_zhou: phased rollout: 1) add SDK lint + nightly warnings; 2) publish golden-path and 30-day migration advisory; 3) enable CI blockers for new violations; 4) flip ingest guardrails in a single canary region for 14 days; 5) global enforcement with dashboard and rollback playbook.

sam_kapoor: metric-log-span joins need a stable request identifier. Propose header X-RD-REQ and fallback to trace_id. Also include short_trace (8 chars) in metrics to lower join cardinality.

maria_zhou: agreed. Canonicalization rule: prefer request_id header; else use trace_id. short_trace included in metrics for cheaper joins.

james: mobile/edge SDKs often push raw attrs to proxies which then enrich. How do we keep rules consistent?

maria_zhou: SDKs should do lightweight checks + PII hashing, but canonicalization and final trimming happen at proxy/ingest to centralize behavior. SDKs still enforce linting locally so devs see problems early.

linh_tran: we need alerting when many spans are trimmed; otherwise teams won't notice regressions.

maria_zhou: ingest will emit governance metrics: trimmed_spans_count, trimmed_keys_by_team, trimmed_top_keys. Alerts: sudden spike in trimmed_spans or any tenant exceeding 1% trimmed -> page oncall. Weekly reports per-product with pre/post migration telemetry stats.

sam_kapoor: add a tiny example SDK lint rule for the repo? Helps adoption.

maria_zhou: done. Pseudocode below:
```js
// SDK lint pseudocode
if (attrName.match(/email|phone|ssn/)) {
  warn('PII detected - hash or remove');
}
if (estimated_cardinality(attrName) > 500) {
  error('High cardinality attribute: ' + attrName);
}
```

devops-bot: feature flag created: ingest.attr_guardrails.v1 default=false owners=@maria_zhou,@sam_kapoor.

james: next steps for eng-platform: draft the RFC with enforcement matrix, sampling interaction details, and the migration timeline. I'll pair with @maria_zhou on governance dashboard mocks.

maria_zhou: will draft RFC today and tag teams. Tradeoff recap: narrowed flexibility for instrumentation up front vs predictable costs and accurate tenant billing later. :thumbsup:
